name: Tick (Ixodes scapularis)
short_description: The only animal in the atlas: an adult Ixodes scapularis (blacklegged/deer tick), a hard tick with a fused idiosoma, no separate head, EIGHT legs, and barbed mouthparts on a forward capitulum. Vector, not a pathogen.

textbook.1: ✅ PASS — fused idiosoma, small forward capitulum with visible chelicerae hooks, small anterior scutum (female form), cutaway shows internal anatomy; EXACTLY EIGHT legs (4+4, confirmed on a 100px grid overlay), all attached to the front half of the body; no antennae, no insect head, no eyes on the scutum.

sem.1: ❌ FAIL — read as an ordinary natural-colour macro photograph rather than a false-colour SEM, and the scutum showed a radiating fan/pleat groove pattern that reads as ornamentation/festoons — scientifically wrong for the eyeless, inornate, festoon-less genus Ixodes.
sem.2: ✅ PASS — clearly artificial false-colour palette (violet-blue idiosoma rim, warm gold scutum), smooth glossy scutum with no fan pattern, crisp SEM surface texture; EXACTLY EIGHT legs fully in frame, mouthparts (hypostome teeth, chelicerae) visible at the capitulum, no eyes.

3d.1: ✅ PASS — natural reddish-brown biological tones (not neon, not monochrome), distinct anterior scutum vs abdomen, fused idiosoma with no separate head; EXACTLY EIGHT legs (4+4, confirmed on grid overlay) attached to the front half of the body; front leg pair held slightly raised (plausible questing pose).

watercolor.1: ✅ PASS — warm cream aged paper fills the frame edge-to-edge with a soft dark wash halo behind the subject and no border/frame/sheet-on-surface look, matching the cocci/rod-bacterium house style; single specimen, fine ink linework, EXACTLY EIGHT legs (4+4, confirmed on grid overlay), small anterior scutum distinct from the abdomen, no antennae or insect head.

reference: ✅ PASS — CDC PHIL #1669 macro photograph of a single unfed adult female Ixodes scapularis in dorsal questing posture on a grass blade; public domain; genus/species confirmed by CDC source metadata; clean single specimen, no baked-in text or scale bar.
